question: 400 mangoes were bought at ₹1220 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹820. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of mangoes.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price of 1 mango = 1220 ÷ 100 = ₹12.2

Profit on 1 mango = 820 ÷ 400 = ₹2.05

Selling Price of 1 mango = 12.2 + 2.05 = ₹14.25

Selling Price per dozen (12 mangoes) = 14.25 × 12 = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of mangoes bought = 400

Cost of 100 mangoes = ₹1220

Total profit on selling all mangoes = ₹820

1 dozen = 12 mangoes

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit

 
 
 
 Total CP = ₹4880
 Profit = ₹820
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Total SP = ₹5700

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) of 400 mangoes = (1220 ÷ 100) × 400 = ₹4880

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) of 400 mangoes = Total CP + Total Profit

⇒ Total SP = 4880 + 820 = ₹5700

⇒ Selling Price of 1 mango = 5700 ÷ 400 = ₹14.25

⇒ Selling Price of 1 dozen mangoes = 14.25 × 12 = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). The actual profit amount is calculated as: Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage

Profit percentage is calculated on the base of Cost Price unless stated otherwise. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method

It is an essential technique in arithmetic where the value of a single unit is found first, which is then multiplied to find the value of the required number of units (like finding the cost of 1 dozen from 1 piece).
